reviewNote: spotless vs pristine are close; pristine adds a sense of untouched freshness.

words.definition: Neat and arranged in good order.
words.example: Please keep your desk tidy.
words.whyHere: The mildest: things are orderly, though not always deeply cleaned.

words.definition: Free from dirt or marks.
words.example: The kitchen floor is clean now.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tidy': dirt has actually been removed.

words.definition: Perfectly clean, with no marks at all.
words.example: Her white shirt stayed spotless all day.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'clean': not a single mark remains.

words.definition: Fresh and completely clean, as if brand new.
words.example: The hotel room looked pristine when we arrived.
words.whyHere: The peak: flawlessly clean and untouched.

reviewNote: eager vs enthusiastic are close; enthusiastic stresses visible energy.

words.definition: Wanting to do something and interested in it.
words.example: She is keen to start the new project.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a quiet, willing interest.

words.definition: Wanting very much to do something.
words.example: The children were eager to open their gifts.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'keen': the wish clearly shows.

words.definition: Showing great excitement and interest.
words.example: He was enthusiastic about the whole plan.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'eager': open, energetic excitement.

words.definition: Extremely eager, often intensely so.
words.example: The zealous fans waited all night outside.
words.whyHere: The peak: eagerness so strong it drives action.

reviewNote: strike vs pound are close; pound adds repeated, heavy force.

words.definition: To hit something lightly and quickly.
words.example: She began to tap the table with a pen.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a soft, gentle touch.

words.definition: To bring your hand or an object against something.
words.example: He tried to hit the ball hard.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tap': real force behind the contact.

words.definition: To hit something with a firm, deliberate blow.
words.example: Lightning can strike a tall tree.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'hit': a sharp, forceful blow.

words.definition: To hit something hard again and again.
words.example: They could hear him pound on the door.
words.whyHere: The peak: heavy, repeated, powerful blows.

reviewNote: fearless vs heroic are close; heroic adds admired, self-sacrificing courage.

words.definition: Willing to take risks and act with confidence.
words.example: She made a bold choice to travel alone.
words.whyHere: The mildest: confident, but not truly tested by danger.

words.definition: Ready to face danger or pain.
words.example: The brave child was not scared of the dark.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'bold': facing real fear or danger.

words.definition: Showing no fear at all.
words.example: The fearless climber scaled the icy cliff.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'brave': fear seems entirely absent.

words.definition: Very brave, in a way people admire.
words.example: Firefighters made a heroic rescue from the flames.
words.whyHere: The peak: bravery great enough to be celebrated.

reviewNote: scrumptious vs delectable are close; both describe extremely tasty food.

words.definition: Having a pleasant taste.
words.example: We ate a tasty bowl of soup.
words.whyHere: The mildest: simply nice to eat.

words.definition: Very pleasant to taste.
words.example: The cake was absolutely delicious.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tasty': clearly a treat.

words.definition: Extremely tasty and enjoyable.
words.example: They served a scrumptious homemade pie.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'delicious': rich, mouth-filling flavour.

words.definition: So delicious it delights you.
words.example: The chef prepared a delectable dessert.
words.whyHere: The peak: about as tasty as food can be.

reviewNote: stinking vs putrid are close; putrid adds the smell of rot.

words.definition: Smelling stale and slightly damp.
words.example: The old cellar smelled musty.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a dull, stale smell rather than a strong stink.

words.definition: Having an unpleasant smell.
words.example: He threw his smelly socks in the wash.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'musty': clearly unpleasant to the nose.

words.definition: Having a strong, very bad smell.
words.example: They walked past a stinking rubbish bin.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'smelly': a powerful, offensive odour.

words.definition: Rotten and smelling terrible.
words.example: The putrid meat had to be thrown away.
words.whyHere: The peak: the foul smell of decay.

reviewNote: shatter vs pulverize are close; pulverize means reduced all the way to powder.

words.definition: To break so that a line appears, but not into pieces.
words.example: The heat can crack a glass dish.
words.whyHere: The mildest: damaged, but still in one piece.

words.definition: To separate into pieces, often suddenly.
words.example: Be careful not to break the plate.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'crack': it comes apart.

words.definition: To break violently into many pieces.
words.example: The ball can smash a window easily.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'break': sudden, forceful destruction.

words.definition: To break suddenly into very small pieces.
words.example: The mirror can shatter into tiny shards.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'smash': it bursts into fragments.

words.definition: To crush something completely into powder or dust.
words.example: The machine can pulverize rock into fine dust.
words.whyHere: The peak: broken down into nothing but powder.

reviewNote: sob vs wail are close; wail adds a loud, drawn-out sound.

words.definition: To make small, weak crying sounds.
words.example: The puppy began to whimper softly.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a quiet, low sound of distress.

words.definition: To shed tears, often with sound.
words.example: The baby started to cry for milk.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'whimper': clear, open weeping.

words.definition: To cry loudly while catching your breath.
words.example: She began to sob at the sad news.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'cry': heavy, shaking tears.

words.definition: To cry out with a long, loud sound.
words.example: The mourners began to wail with grief.
words.whyHere: The peak: loud, uncontrolled crying.

reviewNote: difficult, tough and demanding are close; ranked by rising effort and strain.

words.definition: Needing care and skill to do.
words.example: Parking here can be tricky.
words.whyHere: The mildest: fiddly, but manageable with care.

words.definition: Not easy to do or understand.
words.example: The exam had a difficult final question.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tricky': real effort is needed.

words.definition: Very hard to do and demanding effort.
words.example: Losing the match was a tough moment.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'difficult': testing and hard going.

words.definition: Needing a lot of time, effort, or skill.
words.example: She has a demanding new job.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tough': it constantly asks a lot of you.

words.definition: Extremely hard and exhausting.
words.example: The runners finished a grueling mountain race.
words.whyHere: The peak: so hard it wears you out completely.

reviewNote: baffled vs bewildered are close; bewildered adds a lost, overwhelmed feeling.

words.definition: A little confused and trying to understand.
words.example: He gave a puzzled look at the map.
words.whyHere: The mildest: mildly unsure, still thinking it through.

words.definition: Unable to understand or think clearly.
words.example: The new rules left me confused.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'puzzled': clearly unable to follow.

words.definition: Completely unable to understand something.
words.example: The strange noise left them baffled.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'confused': totally stuck for an answer.

words.definition: So confused that you feel lost.
words.example: The tourist looked bewildered in the busy station.
words.whyHere: The peak: confusion strong enough to overwhelm.

reviewNote: fling vs hurl are close; hurl adds the greatest force.

words.definition: To throw something gently in a high curve.
words.example: She can lob the ball over the net.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a soft, arcing toss.

words.definition: To throw something lightly or carelessly.
words.example: He likes to toss his keys onto the table.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'lob': a casual, easy throw.

words.definition: To send something through the air with your hand.
words.example: Please throw the ball to me.
words.whyHere: The plain, neutral word for sending something flying.

words.definition: To throw something with force and little care.
words.example: Do not fling your bag on the floor.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'throw': fast and forceful.

words.definition: To throw something very hard.
words.example: Waves can hurl stones onto the beach.
words.whyHere: The peak: the most violent, powerful throw.

reviewNote: doze vs nap are close; nap suggests a deliberate short sleep.

words.definition: To sleep lightly for a short time.
words.example: He likes to doze in his armchair.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a light, drifting sleep.

words.definition: To sleep for a short while, usually in the day.
words.example: The baby will nap after lunch.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'doze': a real, chosen short sleep.

words.definition: To rest with your eyes closed and mind unaware.
words.example: I try to sleep eight hours each night.
words.whyHere: The full, normal state of rest.

words.definition: To sleep, especially deeply and peacefully.
words.example: The whole house was in deep slumber.
words.whyHere: The peak: long, deep, peaceful sleep.

reviewNote: hilarious vs uproarious are close; uproarious stresses loud, shared laughter.

words.definition: Making you smile or mildly laugh.
words.example: She told an amusing little story.
words.whyHere: The mildest: pleasant and lightly funny.

words.definition: Causing laughter.
words.example: The film was really funny.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'amusing': it clearly makes you laugh.

words.definition: Extremely funny.
words.example: His joke was absolutely hilarious.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'funny': it brings big laughter.

words.definition: So funny it causes loud laughter.
words.example: The comedy show was uproarious from start to finish.
words.whyHere: The peak: funny enough to make a whole room roar.

reviewNote: yank vs wrench are close; wrench adds a violent twisting force.

words.definition: To pull something with a short, quick movement.
words.example: I felt someone tug at my sleeve.
words.whyHere: The mildest: a small, quick pull.

words.definition: To move something toward you using force.
words.example: Please pull the door to open it.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'tug': a steady, real pull.

words.definition: To pull something suddenly and hard.
words.example: He tried to yank the rope free.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'pull': sharp and sudden.

words.definition: To pull or twist something violently.
words.example: She had to wrench the lid off the jar.
words.whyHere: The peak: a hard, twisting, forceful pull.

reviewNote: serene vs tranquil are close; tranquil stresses complete stillness.

words.definition: Not excited, nervous, or upset.
words.example: She stayed calm during the storm.
words.whyHere: The mildest: simply steady and unbothered.

words.definition: Quiet and free from worry or noise.
words.example: We spent a peaceful evening at home.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'calm': a settled, restful quiet.

words.definition: Very calm, clear, and untroubled.
words.example: The lake looked serene at sunrise.
words.whyHere: Stronger than 'peaceful': a deep, graceful calm.

words.definition: Completely calm and still.
words.example: They found a tranquil spot by the river.
words.whyHere: The peak: perfectly calm and undisturbed.
